text:
Kirill Kaprizov has 49 points in 26 games and a 15-game point streak, and over that run he has turned into a passer: 24 assists to 8 goals. The Wild have points in 15 straight too, and Michael Russo has been waxing poetic about the line with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy. Monday in San Jose he had four more.

How much of it holds? The talent is not in question. He drives play (56% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 6.3 points better than without him), he carries the puck in rather than dumping it, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and he ranks sixth in the league in wins added by goals. But the last ten games produced 24 points where we'd expect about 15, the chances around him are normal, and he's shooting 25% against 17% last season. The Wild have scored 16.6 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our range still projects 107 to 135 points. That's a monster season even after the luck leaks out.
